rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’anic statement about clear proofs is voiced by the Prophet, as its ending says he is not a guardian over the people.
rows.anchor: فإن هذا ورد على لسانه صلى الله عليه وسلم لقوله آخرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about seeking a judge besides God is likewise spoken on the Prophet’s tongue.
rows.anchor: فإنه أوردها أيضا على لسانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that the angels descend only by their Lord’s command is spoken by Gabriel.
rows.anchor: الآية وارد على لسان جبريل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declarations about the angels’ assigned stations, ranks, and glorification are spoken by the angels themselves.
rows.anchor: المسبحون ) وارد على لسان الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worshippers speak this supplication; an implied “say” can be supplied, as with the two earlier human utterances, unlike Gabriel’s and the angels’ speech.
rows.anchor: إلا أنه يمكن هنا تقدير القول أي قولوا وكذا الآيتان الأوليان يصح أن يقدر فيهما قل بخلاف الثالثة والرابعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two statements voiced by the Prophet can be read with an implied command “say”; the later angelic utterances cannot.
rows.anchor: وكذا الآيتان الأوليان يصح أن يقدر فيهما قل بخلاف الثالثة والرابعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fatiha is also called al-Nur, al-Hamd, al-Shukr, al-Hamd al-Ula, and al-Hamd al-Qusra.
rows.anchor: ثاني عشرها وثالث عشرها سورة الحمد وسورة الشكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fatiha is named al-Ruqya, al-Shifa, and al-Shafiya in view of reports about its special virtues.
rows.anchor: سادس عشرها وسابع عشرها وثامن عشرها الرقية والشفاء والشافية للأحاديث الآتية في نوع الخواص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is called the Surah of Prayer because prayer depends on it.
rows.anchor: تاسع عشرها سورة الصلاة لتوقف الصلاة عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is also said to be called al-Salah, as in the hadith “I divided the prayer between Me and My servant,” where “the prayer” means this surah.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن من أسمائها الصلاة أيضا لحديث قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين أي السورة

rows.speaker: المرسي
rows.claim: Al-Mursi explains the name al-Salah as naming the surah after something necessary to it, namely prayer.
rows.anchor: قال المرسي لأنها من لوازمها فهو من باب تسمية الشيء باسم لازمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The name Surah of Supplication reflects the request for guidance it contains.
rows.anchor: الحادي والعشرون سورة الدعاء لاشتمالها عليه

rows.speaker: الإمام فخر الدين
rows.claim: Fakhr al-Din also gives it the name Surah of Asking because it contains a request.
rows.anchor: الثاني والعشرون سورة السؤال لذلك ذكره الإمام فخر الدين

rows.speaker: المرسي
rows.claim: Al-Mursi calls it the Surah of Teaching the Request because it models supplication etiquette by beginning with praise.
rows.anchor: الثالث والعشرون سورة تعليم المسألة قال المرسي لأن فيها آداب السؤال لأنها بدئت بالثناء قبله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is the Surah of Intimate Discourse because the servant privately addresses the Lord in this verse.
rows.anchor: الرابع والعشرون سورة المناجاة لأن العبد يناجي فيها ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is the Surah of Entrusting because the verse expresses reliance and entrusting oneself to God.
rows.anchor: الخامس والعشرون سورة التفويض لاشتمالها عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says this collection of Fatiha names had not previously been gathered in a book.
rows.anchor: فهذا ما وقفت عليه من أسمائها ولم تجتمع في كتاب قبل هذا

rows.speaker: خالد بن معدان
rows.claim: Khalid ibn Ma‘dan called al-Baqara the Fustat of the Qur’an; the source connects the title with its magnitude and its uniquely extensive rulings.
rows.anchor: كان خالد بن معدان يسميها فسطاط القرآن وورد في حديث مرفوع في مسند الفردوس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report in al-Mustadrak calls al-Baqara the summit of the Qur’an, since a summit is the highest part of a thing.
rows.anchor: وفي حديث المستدرك تسميتها سنام القرآن وسنام كل شيء أعلاه

rows.speaker: أبو عطاف
rows.claim: Abu ‘Attaf, in a report in Sa‘id ibn Mansur’s Sunan, says Aal Imran is called Ṭayba in the Torah.
rows.anchor: روى سعيد بن منصور في سننه عن أبي عطاف قال اسم آل عمران في التوراة طيبة

rows.speaker: صحيح مسلم
rows.claim: Sahih Muslim calls al-Baqara and Aal Imran the two radiant surahs.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيح مسلم تسميتها والبقرة الزهراوين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ma’ida is also called al-Uqud and al-Munqida.
rows.anchor: والمائدة تسمى أيضا العقود والمنقذة قال ابن الغرس

rows.speaker: ابن الغرس
rows.claim: Ibn al-Ghars explains al-Munqida as the surah that saves its companion from the angels of punishment.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الغرس لأنها تنقذ صاحبها من ملائكة العذاب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a report from Sa‘id ibn Jubayr, Ibn Abbas identifies al-Anfal as the Surah of Badr.
rows.anchor: أخرج أبو الشيخ عن سعيد بن جبير قال قلت لابن عباس سورة الأنفال قال تلك سورة بدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Surah Bara’a is also called al-Tawba, drawing its name from the verse saying God turned toward the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وبراءة تسمى أيضا التوبة لقوله فيها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas calls it al-Fadiha because repeated revelations naming groups among them made the Companions fear that everyone would be exposed.
rows.anchor: أخرج البخاري عن سعيد بن جبير قال قلت لابن عباس سورة التوبة قال التوبة بل هي الفاضحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pause can be complete under one interpretation, parsing, or reading and incomplete under another; this pause is complete if what follows begins anew, but not if it is conjoined.
rows.anchor: قال وقد يكون الوقف تاما في تفسير وإعراب وقراءة غير تام على آخر نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Stopping at the surah openings is complete if they are parsed as a subject with omitted predicate or as the object of an implied “say,” but incomplete if the following words are their predicate.
rows.anchor: ونحو فواتح السور الوقف عليها تام إن أعربت مبتدأ والخبر محذوف أو عكسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stop after “a place of return and security” is complete with the kasra reading of “and take,” but only sufficient with its fatḥa reading.
rows.anchor: ونحو ﴿ مثابة للناس وأمنا ﴾ تام على قراءة ﴿ واتخذوا ﴾ بكسر الخاء كاف على قراءة الفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stop after “to the path of the Mighty, the Praiseworthy” is complete if the following divine name is nominative, and good if genitive.
rows.anchor: ونحو ﴿ إلى صراط العزيز الحميد ﴾ تام على قراءة من رفع الاسم الكريم بعدها حسن على قراءة من خفض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both stops are complete, but the stop after “Master of the Day of Judgment” is more complete because the next clause shares the direct address, unlike the first.
rows.anchor: كلاهما تام إلا أن الأول أتم من الثاني لاشتراك الثاني فيما بعده في معنى الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some call the less complete of two complete stops “resembling complete.”
rows.anchor: وهذا هو الذي سماه بعضهم شبيها بالتام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A “necessary” stop is strongly recommended to make the intended meaning clear, even though a relation to what follows remains.
rows.anchor: ومنه ما يتأكد استحسانه لبيان المعنى المقصود به وهو الذي سماه السجاوندي باللازم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A stop attached to what follows only by meaning is called sufficient: each side is independently complete; the cited examples include the spending clause, what was sent before, and “upon guidance.”
rows.anchor: وهو المسمى بالكافي للاكتفاء به واستغنائه عما بعده واستغناء ما بعده عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sufficient pauses can differ in degree: “in their hearts is a disease” is sufficient, “God increased their disease” more so, and the clause about their lying most sufficient.
rows.anchor: ويتفاضل في الكفاية كتفاضل التام نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stop after “they teach people sorcery” is sufficient if the following “what” is negative, but merely good if it is a relative pronoun.
rows.anchor: وقد يكون الوقف كافيا على تفسير وإعراب وقراءة غير كاف على آخر نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stop after “they are certain of the Hereafter” is sufficient if the next words start a new sentence, but only good if they predicate the preceding believers clause.
rows.anchor: ﴿ وبالآخرة هم يوقنون ﴾ كاف إن أعرب ما بعده مبتدأ خبره ﴿ على هدى ﴾ حسن إن جعل خبر ﴿ الذين يؤمنون بالغيب ﴾ أو خبر ﴿ والذين يؤمنون بما أنزل ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The stop after “we are sincere to Him” is sufficient with the direct-address reading “or do you say,” but only good with the third-person reading.
rows.anchor: ﴿ ونحن له مخلصون ﴾ كاف على قراءة ﴿ أم تقولون ﴾ بالخطاب حسن على قراءة الغيب

rows.speaker: أهل البيان
rows.claim: Rhetoricians generally say fronting an object, adverbial, or prepositional phrase conveys restriction; thus the verse means that worship and help are directed to God alone.
rows.anchor: كاد أهل البيان يطبقون على أن تقديم المعمول يفيد الحصر سواء كان مفعولا أو ظرفا أو مجرورا ولهذا قيل في

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause puts “over you” first to restrict whose testimony is meant; “over people” is delayed because the point there is simply to establish the community’s testimony.
rows.anchor: أخرت الصلة في الشهادة الأولى وقدمت في الثانية لأن الغرض في الأول إثبات شهادتهم وفي الثاني إثبات اختصاصهم بشهادة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عليهم

rows.speaker: ابن الحاجب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Hajib rejects the usual restrictive reading of a fronted complement as an illusion, citing the command to worship God sincerely and then the fronted “rather, worship God.”
rows.anchor: وخالف في ذلك ابن الحاجب فقال في شرح المفصل الاختصاص الذي يتوهمه كثير من الناس من تقديم المعمول وهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author answers that “sincerely devoting religion to Him” already implies restriction; even without it, a clause may name the restricted object without restrictive syntax, while “rather worship God” strongly implies exclusivity after the warning against shirk.
rows.anchor: أغنى عن إفادة الحصر في الآية الأولى ولو لم يكن فما المانع من ذكر المحصور في محل بغير صيغة الحصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the preceding verse warns that shirk would nullify the Prophet’s work, “rather, worship God” is among the strongest evidence for exclusive worship; without exclusivity, “rather” would not mark a contrast.
rows.anchor: من أقوى أدلة الإختصاص فإن قبلها

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan challenges the restrictive interpretation with the question asking whether the audience commands worship of someone other than God.
rows.anchor: واعترض أبو حيان على مدعي الإختصاص بنحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply is that association of other gods made it as though they did not worship God; their call to shirk was equivalent to telling them to worship only another.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأنه لما أشرك بالله غيره كأنه لم يعبد الله وكان أمرهم بالشرك كأنه أمر بتخصيص غير الله بالعبادة

words: كلا هدينا ونوحا هدينا من قبل
rows.speaker: صاحب الفلك الدائر
rows.claim: The author of al-Falak al-Da’ir rejects restriction by citing “all We guided, and Noah We guided before,” one of the strongest objections.
rows.anchor: ورد صاحب الفلك الدائر الإختصاص بقوله

words: كلا هدينا ونوحا هدينا من قبل
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reply is that fronting conveys restriction as a general tendency, not an invariable entailment, so an exceptional instance does not disprove the rule.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأنه لا يدعى فيه اللزوم بل الغلبة وقد يخرج الشيء عن الغالب

words: أغير الله تدعون إن كنتم صادقين
rows.speaker: الشيخ بهاء الدين
rows.claim: Baha al-Din says one verse combines fronting without restriction in its first clause and unequivocal restriction in the fronted “Him” in its second.
rows.anchor: قال الشيخ بهاء الدين وقد اجتمع الاختصاص وعدمه في آية واحدة وهي

words: الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse explicitly attributes favor to God, but avoids saying “those with whom You were angry,” shifting expression so anger is not verbally attributed to God in direct address.
rows.anchor: مصرحا بذكر المنعم وإسناد الإنعام إليه لفظا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One explanation says that after God is described as Lord, Merciful, and Master of Judgment, the worshipper addresses Him alone as worthy of worship and reliance.
rows.anchor: وقيل لأنه لما ذكر الحقيق بالحمد وأجرى عليه الصفات العظيمة من كونه ربا للعالمين ورحمانا ورحيما ومالكا ليوم الدين تعلق العلم بمعلوم عظيم الشأن

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A spiritual explanation sees a movement from creatures’ initial distance and inability to converse with God to readiness for intimate address after knowing, praising, and worshipping Him.
rows.anchor: ومن لطائفه التنبيه على أن مبتدأ الخلق الغيبة منهم عنه سبحانه وتعالى وقصورهم عن محاضرته ومخاطبته وقيام حجاب العظمة عليهم

rows.speaker: ابن الأثير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Athir calls this transition a form of separation better than conjunction: a strong connection between moving from one kind of speech to another.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأثير هذا في هذا المقام من الفصل الذي هو أحسن من الوصل وهي علاقة أكيدة بين الخروج من كلام إلى آخر

rows.speaker: الزنجاني والطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Zanjani and al-Tibi define a good transition to the request as stating the means before reaching the intended aim; the verse moves from praise to the request for help and guidance.
rows.anchor: قال الزنجاني والطيبي وهو أن يخرج إلى الغرض بعد تقدم الوسيلة

words: فإنهم عدو لي إلا رب العالمين
رب هب لي حكما وألحقني بالصالحين
rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Tibi says Abraham’s speech combines a graceful transition and a good request: he moves from God’s attributes to “My Lord, grant me judgment and join me with the righteous.”
rows.anchor: قال الطيبي ومما اجتمع فيه حسن التخلص والمطلب معا قوله تعالى حكاية عن إبراهيم

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says the Fatiha encompasses praise, worship through commands and prohibitions, and promise and warning; every Qur’anic verse falls under one of these topics.
rows.anchor: وبيان اشتمالها على علوم القرآن قرره الزمخشري باشتمالها على الثناء على الله تعالى بما هو أهله وعلى التعبد بالأمر والنهي وعلى الوعد والوعيد

rows.speaker: الإمام فخر الدين
rows.claim: Fakhr al-Din maps the Qur’an’s four aims—God, resurrection, prophethood, and divine decree—onto the Fatiha: praise, Judgment Day, worship and reliance, and guidance through the surah’s end; this supports its name Umm al-Qur’an.
rows.anchor: وقال الإمام فخر الدين المقصود من القرآن كله تقرير أمور أربعة الإلهيات والمعاد والنبوات وإثبات القضاء والقدر لله تعالى

rows.speaker: البيضاوي
rows.claim: Al-Baydawi says the Fatiha contains theoretical wisdom, practical rulings in walking the straight path, and knowledge of the ranks of the blessed and abodes of the wretched.
rows.anchor: وقال البيضاوي هي مشتملة على الحكم النظرية والأحكام العملية التي هي سلوك الطريق المستقيم والاطلاع على مراتب السعداء ومنازل الأشقياء

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Tibi divides the Fatiha’s religious knowledge into foundations (God and attributes, prophethood, resurrection), branches (worship), ethical perfection and seeking the path, and accounts of earlier peoples with promise and threat.
rows.anchor: وقال الطيبي هي مشتملة على أربعة أنواع من العلوم التي هي مناط الدين

rows.speaker: الغزالي
rows.claim: Al-Ghazali lists three essential Qur’anic aims—knowing God, the straight path, and the return in the Hereafter—and three supplementary aims: the obedient, deniers’ speech, and the stations of the path, all signaled by the Fatiha.
rows.anchor: وقال الغزالي مقاصد القرآن سنة ثلاثة مهمة وثلاثة متمة الأولى تعريف المدعو إليه كما أشير إليه بصدرها

rows.speaker: الزركشي وناصر الدين بن الميلق
rows.claim: They reconcile the hadith calling the Fatiha two-thirds of the Qur’an by saying it indicates all Qur’anic aims through inclusion and implication, but not direct correspondence; those are two of three modes of indication.
rows.anchor: ذكره الزركشي في شرح التنبيه وناصر الدين بن الميلق قال وأيضا الحقوق ثلاثة حق الله على عباده

rows.speaker: ناصر الدين بن الميلق
rows.claim: A second explanation counts three kinds of rights—God’s claim on servants, servants’ claim on God, and people’s claims on one another—and says the Fatiha explicitly covers the first two, hence two-thirds.
rows.anchor: قال وأيضا الحقوق ثلاثة حق الله على عباده وحق العباد على الله وحق بعض العباد على بعض وقد اشتملت الفاتحة صريحا على الحقين الأولين فناسب كونها بصريحها ثلثين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hadith “I divided the prayer between Me and My servant in two halves” supports the Fatiha’s two-thirds description.
rows.anchor: وحديث ( قسمت الصلاة بيني وبين عبدي نصفين ) شاهد لذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no conflict between hadiths calling the Fatiha the greatest surah and al-Baqara the greatest: al-Baqara is greatest among surahs other than the Fatiha because of its detailed laws, parables, and arguments.
rows.anchor: قلت ولا تنافي أيضا بين كون الفاتحة أعظم السور وبين الحديث الآخر أن البقرة أعظم السور

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi quotes a teacher saying the Fatiha contains a thousand commands, prohibitions, rulings, and reports; Ibn Umar spent eight years teaching it because of its jurisprudential depth.
rows.anchor: قال ابن العربي في أحكامه سمعت بعض أشياخي يقول فيها ألف أمر وألف نهي وألف حكم وألف خبر

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says the Throne Verse is the greatest verse because of the greatness of its meaning, since a thing’s honor follows its essence, import, and relations.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن العربي أيضا إنما صارت آية الكرسي أعظم الآيات لعظم مقتضاها فإن الشيء إنما يشرف بشرف ذاته ومقتضاه وتعلقاته

rows.speaker: ابن العربي
rows.claim: Ibn al-Arabi likens the Throne Verse among verses to al-Ikhlas among surahs, while saying al-Ikhlas surpasses it in two respects not specified in this excerpt.
rows.anchor: وهي في آي القرآن كسورة الإخلاص في سورة إلا أن سورة الإخلاص تفضلها بوجهين

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali said, as transmitted by Ibn Abi Jamra, that he could load seventy camels with commentary on the Umm al-Qur’an; the source explains the remark by showing how much each phrase requires.
rows.anchor: قال ابن أبي جمرة عن علي رضي الله عنه أنه قال لو شئت أوقر سبعين بعيرا من تفسير أم القرآن لفعلت

rows.speaker: ابن أبي جمرة
rows.claim: Explaining the scale of commentary, Ibn Abi Jamra says the opening requires explaining praise, the divine name and transcendence, and the worlds, their nature, types, number, and extent.
rows.anchor: يحتاج تبيين معنى الحمد وما يتعلق به الاسم الجليل الذي هو الله وما يليق به من التنزيه ثم يحتاج إلى بيان العالم وكيفيته

rows.speaker: ابن أبي جمرة
rows.claim: Commentary on the two divine names must explain their meanings and majesty, all the divine names and attributes, and why these two are used at this point.
rows.anchor: يحتاج إلى بيان الاسمين الجليلين وما يليق بهما من الجلال وما معناهما ثم يحتاج إلى بيان جميع الأسماء والصفات

rows.speaker: ابن أبي جمرة
rows.claim: Explaining “Master of the Day of Judgment” entails describing that Day, its stations and terrors, and where its people will settle.
rows.anchor: يحتاج إلى بيان ذلك اليوم وما فيه من المواطن والأهوال وكيفية مستقره

rows.speaker: ابن أبي جمرة
rows.claim: Commentary on the verse requires explaining God’s majesty, worship, its forms and performance, the worshipper’s qualities, and the nature and manner of seeking aid.
rows.anchor: يحتاج إلى بيان المعبود من جلالته والعبادة وكيفيتها وصفتها وأدائها على جميع أنواعها والعابد في صفته

rows.speaker: ابن أبي جمرة
rows.claim: The closing request requires explaining guidance and the straight path and its opposites, the angered and astray and their qualities, and the approved people and their way.
rows.anchor: يحتاج إلى بيان الهداية ما هي والصراط المستقيم وأضداده وتبيين المغضوب عليهم والضالين وصفاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says huda has seventeen senses, beginning with steadfastness in the request to be guided on the straight path; his list in fact contains eighteen numbered senses.
rows.anchor: 1 بمعنى الثبات ﴿ اهدنا الصراط المستقيم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huda can mean clarification or explanation.
rows.anchor: 2 والبيان ﴿ أولئك على هدى من ربهم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huda can mean religion.
rows.anchor: 3 والدين ﴿ إن الهدى هدى الله ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huda can mean faith.
rows.anchor: 4 والإيمان ﴿ ويزيد الله الذين اهتدوا هدى ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huda can mean supplication, as in “a guide for every people” and “leaders who guide by Our command.”
rows.anchor: 5 والدعاء ﴿ ولكل قوم هاد ﴾ ﴿ وجعلناهم أئمة يهدون بأمرنا ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huda can mean the messengers and scriptures sent by God.
rows.anchor: 6 وبمعنى الرسل والكتب ﴿ فإما يأتينكم مني هدى ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huda can mean knowledge, as in being guided by the stars.
rows.anchor: 7 والمعرفة ﴿ وبالنجم هم يهتدون ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huda can refer to the Prophet himself.
rows.anchor: 8 وبمعنى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ﴿ إن الذين يكتمون ما أنزلنا من البينات والهدى ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huda can mean the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: 9 وبمعنى القرآن ﴿ ولقد جاءهم من ربهم الهدى ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huda can mean the Torah, in the verse about what was given to Moses.
rows.anchor: 10 والتوراة ﴿ ولقد آتينا موسى الهدى ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huda can mean the formula of returning to God (istirja’).
rows.anchor: 11 والاسترجاع ﴿ وأولئك هم المهتدون ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the passage about Abraham’s dispute, huda means a proof or argument: God does not give the wrongdoers an argument.
rows.anchor: 12 والحجة ﴿ لا يهدي القوم الظالمين ﴾ بعد قوله تعالى ﴿ ألم تر إلى الذي حاج إبراهيم في ربه ﴾ أي لا يهديهم حجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huda can mean monotheism.
rows.anchor: 13 والتوحيد ﴿ إن نتبع الهدى معك ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huda can mean the Sunna or exemplary practice.
rows.anchor: 14 والسنة ﴿ فبهداهم اقتده ﴾ ﴿ وإنا على آثارهم مهتدون ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huda can mean rectification or setting aright.
rows.anchor: 15 والإصلاح ﴿ وأن الله لا يهدي كيد الخائنين ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “He gave each thing its form, then guided it,” huda means inspiration about how to secure a livelihood.
rows.anchor: 16 والإلهام ﴿ أعطى كل شيء خلقه ثم هدى ﴾ أي ألهمهم المعاش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huda can mean repentance.
rows.anchor: 17 والتوبة ﴿ إنا هدنا إليك ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Huda can mean showing or directing someone to the right way.
rows.anchor: 18 والإرشاد ﴿ أن يهديني سواء السبيل ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word su’ can mean severity, as in “severe punishment.”
rows.anchor: 1 الشدة ﴿ يسومونكم سوء العذاب ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Su’ can mean harm or injury, as in the prohibition on touching the she-camel with harm.
rows.anchor: 2 والعقر ﴿ ولا تمسوها بسوء ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Su’ can mean sexual misconduct, as in the two quoted examples.
rows.anchor: 3 والزنى ﴿ ما جزاء من أراد بأهلك سوءا ﴾ ﴿ ما كان أبوك امرأ سوء ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Su’ can refer to leprosy, as in the sign of a hand white without disease.
rows.anchor: 4 والبرص ﴿ بيضاء من غير سوء ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Su’ can mean punishment.
rows.anchor: 5 والعذاب ﴿ إن الخزي اليوم والسوء ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Su’ can mean associating partners with God.
rows.anchor: 6 والشرك ﴿ ما كنا نعمل من سوء ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Su’ can mean abusive or evil speech, including speaking it openly and the tongues’ utterance of it.
rows.anchor: 7 والشتم ﴿ لا يحب الله الجهر بالسوء ﴾ ﴿ وألسنتهم بالسوء ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Su’ can mean sin.
rows.anchor: 8 والذنب ﴿ يعملون السوء بجهالة ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Su’ can be used in the sense of “bad” or “wretched,” as in “the evil abode.”
rows.anchor: 9 وبمعنى بئس ﴿ ولهم سوء الدار ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a noun is repeated, four definiteness patterns are possible; when both occurrences are definite, the second usually denotes the first, as with “the straight path, the path of those You favored.”
rows.anchor: فإن كانا معرفتين فالثاني هو الأول غالبا دلالة على المعهود الذي هو في الأصل في اللام أو الإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When both repeated nouns are indefinite, the second usually differs from the first; the three occurrences of weakness denote semen, childhood, and old age.
rows.anchor: وإن كانا نكرتين فالثاني غير الأول غالبا وإلا لكان المناسب هو التعريف بناء على كونه معهودا سابقا

rows.speaker: ابن الحاجب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Hajib says “a month” is repeated to state the duration of the morning and evening journeys separately; words measuring quantities should not be elided, and a pronoun would retain the earlier term’s specific reference.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن الحاجب في قوله تعالى ﴿ غدوها شهر ورواحها شهر ﴾ الفائدة في إعادة لفظ الشهر الإعلام بمقدار زمن الغدو وزمن الرواح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated definite hardship refers to the same hardship, while the indefinite ease is different; the Prophet therefore said one hardship will not overcome two eases.
rows.anchor: فالعسر الثاني هو الأول واليسر الثاني غير الأول ولهذا قال صلى الله عليه وسلم في الآية لن يغلب عسر يسرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When an indefinite noun is followed by a definite one, the latter usually refers back to the former by familiarity, as in “a messenger … the messenger.”
rows.anchor: وإن كان الأول نكرة والثاني معرفة فالثاني هو الأول حملا على العهد نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite noun following an indefinite one likewise refers back to it in the repeated lamp and glass expressions.
rows.anchor: فيها مصباح المصباح في زجاجة الزجاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite possessive “God’s path” refers back to the preceding indefinite “a straight path.”
rows.anchor: إلى صراط مستقيم صراط الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another example of an indefinite followed by its definite antecedent is “no way … the way.”
rows.anchor: ما عليهم من سبيل إنما السبيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a definite noun is followed by an indefinite one, no general rule applies: context can show they differ, as with two senses of “hour,” a requested “book,” and Moses’ “guidance”; al-Zamakhshari distinguishes the latter as all Moses’ religion, miracles, and laws versus guidance.
rows.anchor: وإن كان الأول معرفة والثاني نكرة فلا يطلق القول بل يتوقف على القرائن فتارة تقوم قرينة على التغاير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Context can also show that the definite and following indefinite are the same referent, as when “an Arabic Qur’an” restates “this Qur’an.”
rows.anchor: وتارة تقوم قرينة على الإتحاد نحو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reinforced metaphor is the strongest type: “buying” means choosing or exchanging, then “profit” and “trade” extend the imagery from the source domain.
rows.anchor: فالأولى وهي أبلغها أن تقترن بما يلائم المستعار منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A stripped metaphor is joined to language fitting its target: hunger is called clothing, while “taste” fits the experience; “taste” is more eloquent because it stresses inward pain.
rows.anchor: والثانية أن تقرن بما يلائم المستعار له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A verified metaphor has a sense realized physically or rationally; “the straight path” is the true religion, a concept realized by reason.
rows.anchor: أي الدين الحق فإن كلا منهما يتحقق عقلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A manifest light” is a verified metaphor understood rationally as clear exposition and a compelling proof.
rows.anchor: أي بيانا واضحا وحجة لامعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a metaphor by insinuation, the covenant is implicitly likened to a rope; “undo” signals the unspoken comparison.
rows.anchor: شبه العهد بالحبل وأضمر في النفس فلم يصرح بشيء من أركان التشبيه سوى العهد المشبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse omits fire, the implied source of the comparison, and indicates it through the fire’s characteristic blazing.
rows.anchor: طوى ذكر المشبه به وهو النار ودل عليه بلازمه وهو الاشتعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He made it taste” compares the felt effects of harm and pain to the experience of bitter taste.
rows.anchor: شبه ما يدرك من أثر الضرر والألم بما يدرك من طعم المر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sealing hearts compares their inability to accept truth to an object secured by a seal.
rows.anchor: شبهها في ألا تقبل الحق بالشيء الموثوق المختوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Substitution (badal) clarifies after an ambiguous expression and reinforces it: it restates its meaning as if the governing word were repeated.
rows.anchor: والقصد به الإيضاح بعد الإبهام وفائدته البيان والتأكيد أما الأول فواضح أنك إذا قلت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The path of those You favored” is a whole-for-whole apposition clarifying “the straight path”; the source also gives this construction in other verses, including the repeated forelock phrase.
rows.anchor: مثال الأول ﴿ اهدنا الصراط المستقيم صراط الذين أنعمت عليهم ﴾ ﴿ لتهدي إلى صراط مستقيم صراط الله ﴾ ﴿ لنسفعا بالناصية ناصية كاذبة خاطئة ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Partitive apposition is illustrated by specifying those able to make the pilgrimage and by people repelling one another.
rows.anchor: ومثال الثاني ﴿ ولله على الناس حج البيت من استطاع إليه سبيلا ﴾ ﴿ ولولا دفع الله الناس بعضهم ببعض ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Apposition of inclusion is shown by the forgotten fish episode, fighting in the sacred month, the people of the trench, and houses adorned with silver.
rows.anchor: ومثال الثالث ﴿ وما أنسانيه إلا الشيطان أن أذكره ﴾ ﴿ يسألونك عن الشهر الحرام قتال فيه قل قتال فيه كبير ﴾ ﴿ قتل أصحاب الأخدود النار ﴾ ﴿ لجعلنا لمن يكفر بالرحمن لبيوتهم ﴾

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some add a whole-from-part apposition: “Gardens of Eden” replaces “the Garden” as a part, emphasizing that there are many gardens rather than one.
rows.anchor: وزاد بعضهم بدل الكل من البعض وقد وجدت له مثالا في القرآن وهو قوله

rows.speaker: ابن السيد
rows.claim: Ibn al-Sayyid says some appositions reinforce rather than resolve doubt; without the second “path,” no one would doubt that the straight path is God’s path.
rows.anchor: قال ابن السيد وليس كل بدل يقصد به رفع الإشكال الذي يعرض في المبدل منه بل من البدل ما يراد به التأكيد وإن كان ما قبله غنيا عنه

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh explicitly recognizes apposition whose purpose is reinforcement.
rows.anchor: وقد نص سيبويه على أن من البدل ما الغرض منه التأكيد

rows.speaker: ابن عبد السلام
rows.claim: Ibn Abd al-Salam treats “Azar” as a non-clarifying apposition because “his father” is unambiguous; the reply is that father can also mean grandfather, so the name specifies the biological father.
rows.anchor: قال ولا بيان فيه لأن الأب لا يلتبس بغيره ورد بأنه يطلق على الجد فأبدل لبيان إرادة الأب حقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Fatiha points to all major Qur’anic disciplines: knowledge of God and attributes, prophecy, resurrection, worship, ethical conduct and the straight path, and stories teaching the outcomes of obedience and disobedience.
rows.anchor: وقد وجه ذلك بأن العلوم التي احتوى عليها القرآن قامت بها الأديان أربعة علم الأصول ومداره على معرفة الله وصفاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By signaling all Qur’anic aims, the Fatiha achieves an exemplary opening and combines beautiful words, pleasing cadence, and rhetorical forms.
rows.anchor: فنبه في الفاتحة على جميع مقاصد القرآن وهذا هو الغاية في براعة الاستهلال مع ما اشتملت عليه من الألفاظ الحسنة والمقاطع المستحسنة وأنواع البلاغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening of “Read” similarly previews the Qur’an: it commands reading, begins in God’s name, signals legal knowledge and the principles of religion, and reports God’s teaching of what humans did not know; it can therefore be called the Qur’an’s title.
rows.anchor: وكذلك أول سورة ( اقرأ فإنها مشتملة على نظير ما اشتملت عليه الفاتحة من براعة الاستهلال
